problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Using the Definition
examples.problem:
Suppose $\mathbf{T} : V \rightarrow W$ is a linear map and $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \}$ and $\mathcal{C} = \{ \mathbf{c}_1,\mathbf{c}_2 \}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. Find the matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ of the map $\mathbf{T}$ relative to these bases, if 

$\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1)=-3\mathbf{c}_1+5\mathbf{c}_2,\quad$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2)=\mathbf{c}_2-2\mathbf{c}_1\quad$ and $\quad\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)=\mathbf{c}_1+5\mathbf{c}_2.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we write the images of vectors in $\mathcal{B}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C} \mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1})=-3{c}_{1}+5{c}_{2} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2})={c}_{2}-2{c}_{1} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3})={c}_{1}+5{c}_{2} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1),$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2)$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}\mathbin{:}$
